plannedVideo: How did an earthquake thousands of miles away make waves in a Nevada desert cave?
coldViewerPull: A sheltered pool in a dry landscape seems disconnected from an earthquake across the Pacific. The viewer wants to know what crossed that distance and what actually moved.
expectedPayoff: Seismic energy traveled through Earth and set water already inside the cave sloshing. An apparently isolated pool can register a distant earthquake, and even modest waves can disturb the shallow feeding shelf of a rare fish.

truthEvidenceStatus.framing: How did an earthquake thousands of miles away make waves in a Nevada desert cave? NPS documents minor waves after the July 2025 Kamchatka quake; USGS explains seismic seiches. This is preliminary feasibility, not final exact-claim or visual-causality verification.
caveats: Use seismic seiche, not an ocean tsunami; waves are water already in the cave, not an underwater channel linking Russia and Nevada.
NPS July 2025 report says approximately ten-inch waves and minor disturbance. Do not borrow two-metre heights from other events or imply this event nearly wiped out the pupfish.
NPS gives July 29, 2025; original catalog UTC date/time not inspected. Do not invent a cross-zone event chronology.
The 21 minutes, nearly 4,000 miles and cave dimensions are NPS event-report values, not independently recalculated; exact numerical scope needs final verification.
General USGS mechanism supports feasibility, not a quantitative Devils Hole resonance model, exaggerated ground displacement or exact wave propagation path.

intendedStory: Open on the local disturbance and remote-earthquake question; establish the distant event; distinguish energy propagating through Earth from seawater traveling to Nevada; follow motion into enclosed back-and-forth sloshing; reveal the shallow shelf and its food; return to the pool as a distant-motion indicator with event impact honestly minor.
whySelected: Select the distant-earthquake/Devils Hole story for its immediate place-and-distance surprise and a payoff explaining what traveled, what moved locally, and why even small waves matter. Apollo 12 offers greater acute human stakes; the person-switch story offers direct self-relevance and a memory twist; RNA editing offers molecular wonder. At equal access and cost, the cave story most clearly converts one vivid observation into physical and ecological understanding. This is editorial judgment, not predicted retention, a water/physics preference or renderer convenience.
materialRisks: Do not frame a seismic seiche as an ocean tsunami, imply large July 2025 waves or near-extinction, or portray an underground ocean connection.
